rv.q: Christmas Carol Goes Wrong shows that the company, founded by writers Henry Lewis, Jonathan Sayer and Henry Shields, has certainly mastered its own particular brand of mis-step mayhem with this pacy, slick and hilarious take on the Dickens classic.
The brash, obvious, knockabout humour is laced with moments of lightning-flash wit and invention.
It’s a script that leaves no loose end – every single line has a worthwhile, deliciously funny purpose.
Matt DiCarlo’s production hums with comedic harmony.
These actors know how to fail with a flourish.

Thanks to admirable design work from Libby Todd, it’s impossible not to laugh when a giant box of Maltesers appears in Scrooge’s Victorian counting house, or a Barbie-pink play kitchen pops up in Fred’s home.
It could be sharper, but their fans will love seeing them lay waste to another institution.

This comfort-food entertainment doles out familiar ingredients galore: spotlights crash to the ground and cast-members collide with the scenery (Marley’s ghost even becomes entangled with a four-poster bed).
Ultimately, Christmas Carol Goes Wrong is yet another triumph for Mischief Theatre that is perfect for the holiday season.

Mostly though, this is an irresistible Christmas treat, and it has real heart too: Scrooge-like Chris has an outlook change worthy of Ebenezer himself and in keeping with the spirit of the original Dickens.

Every key moment in Dickens’ original story finds its place in the show, whilst every conceivable mishap and element of mayhem is fused into the storyline in a non-stop and impeccably delivered cacophony of comic capers and chaos.
For fans and newcomers alike, Christmas Carol Goes Wrong is loveably silly, raucous, and highly entertaining.
So as usual Mischief has pulled it off, triumphantly.
For those seeking festive cheer without sentimentality, Cornley’s latest disaster is the Christmas Carol to see.
This is a true Christmassy treat.

cn.t: Mischief's festive farce delivers reliably chaotic laughs with impeccably timed slapstick, though some critics wonder if the formula is wearing thin. Fans of the "Goes Wrong" series will find plenty to enjoy in this Dickensian disaster.

vr.q: If you have any love for these Goes Wrong shows, this one I think is essential.
